title: A sideways goal needs a feasible maneuver
question: Why can the base reach a sideways pose but not slide sideways?
scope: Obstacle-free schematic turn-drive-turn example. Body proportions match the print schematic; coordinates are arbitrary length units. Rotation sweeps clearance; no obstacle or collision guarantee is modeled.

steps.title: Start at the sideways goal offset
steps.explanation: The base faces along positive x; the destination is along positive y.

snapshot.result: The geometric goal does not specify a feasible instantaneous velocity.

steps.title: Test a sideways velocity
steps.explanation: A positive y velocity at zero heading violates the no-slip constraint. The actual pose stays fixed.

snapshot.result: The candidate velocity is rejected; no sideways slip occurs.

transition.meaning: A positive y velocity at zero heading violates the no-slip constraint. The actual pose stays fixed.

steps.title: Turn about the axle center
steps.explanation: Counter-rotating wheels rotate the base while its axle center stays fixed.

snapshot.result: The heading now aligns forward motion with the lateral goal.

transition.meaning: Counter-rotating wheels rotate the base while its axle center stays fixed.

steps.title: Drive forward along the new heading
steps.explanation: Both wheels roll forward; the axle center moves along positive y.

snapshot.result: A lateral displacement has been reached through forward rolling.

transition.meaning: Both wheels roll forward; the axle center moves along positive y.

steps.title: Turn back at the goal
steps.explanation: Counter-rotating wheels restore the original heading without translating the axle center.

snapshot.result: The goal pose is reached by three admissible motions, each requiring space and time.

transition.meaning: Counter-rotating wheels restore the original heading without translating the axle center.

invariants: During each turn the axle center remains fixed.
The rejected sideways candidate never moves the actual base.
Admitted translation follows the heading and has zero no-slip residual.
Footprints are endpoint outlines, not a collision-checked swept hull.

invariants: Force equals plate stiffness times indentation.

title: The load stops before the timing penalty does

scope: The chapter’s illustrative shared-package RC and governor model, not a chip measurement. The same tick cycle count runs at nominal or halved clock; blocking and interference stay fixed. Each displayed tick is a representative completion, not a repeated animation.

tick.status: Schedule geometry changes only when the governor restores the clock

steps.title: Stop proposal inference

transition.meaning: The package cools toward baseline, but the lower clear threshold has not been reached.

invariants: Removing workload does not instantly remove stored thermal energy.

The same instruction work changes duration only because the declared clock changes.
The scheduling period is longer than the deadline; completion inside a period does not prove timely response.
